title: Make four circular controls feel related but unambiguous
summary: Build range, toggle, option, and action controls that share one grammar while preserving distinct behavior on touch and keyboard.
originNote: Distilled from a history-derived circular-control system where gesture arbitration, precision, and perceptible state mattered more than a knob skin.

setup.instructions: Mount the control packet. Build a self-contained touch-first test bench; no hardware haptics or audio are required.

turns.content: Read fixtures/controls.json and implement a complete responsive control test bench as index.html. The four controls must share a circular grammar but make range, boolean, options, and momentary action perceptibly different at rest and during use. At phone width they sit in a horizontally scrollable strip: a horizontal swipe beginning on a control must still be able to scroll the strip, while a deliberate vertical gesture adjusts or actuates that control. Support tap where appropriate, drag end, pointer cancellation, keyboard operation, visible focus, and coarse/fine adjustment for the range. Display an event log so a reviewer can see gesture classification and committed values. Use data-control with values range, boolean, options, and action.

Revise the controls so every committed state remains clear in a still screenshot and under prefers-reduced-motion. Keep the gesture arbitration, keyboard behavior, and chosen visual direction; do not replace the circular family with ordinary sliders and switches.

checks.description: All four control types and cancellation handling are present.
At 390px test strip scrolling, deliberate vertical adjustment, cancellation, keyboard use, and reduced motion.
